why: The start-at-login press's refusals at its backup and at its write (wave 13t, round W26), and, since round W28, a first unit whose file beside it is left and a file where a folder of the unit goes, and, since round W29, a unit kept whose file beside it is left and a unit kept whose copy and file beside it are both left, and the press On in an AppImage, which is refused because a unit would name the folder the AppImage is mounted at, and, since round 2 of package PH-T, the press Off in an AppImage whose unit could not be copied, could not be removed, or was removed while systemd would not read its units again: no door here can safely meet them, because each needs this computer's HOME and systemd, or a server run from an AppImage. tests/the-office-starts-at-login-by-the-persons-press.test.ts meets each with a scratch home and a stand-in systemctl, and the AppImage's with an AppImage folder given to the press; the press Off's removal is met with a stand-in for it.

Test: the unit could not be written, and the file beside it is still there.
Test: the unit could not be written and was kept, and the file beside it is still there.
Test: the unit could not be written and was kept, and its copy and the file beside it are still there.
Test: a file stands where a folder of the unit goes.
Test: this office runs from an AppImage.
Test: the unit was disabled and could not be copied.
Test: the unit was disabled and copied, and could not be removed.
Test: the unit was disabled, copied and removed, and systemd did not read its units again.
